heroLead: North Irwin is a small borough tucked against the bigger town of Irwin along old coal and gas country in Westmoreland County, and the mineral tracts here are often leftovers from farms that got subdivided into house lots two or three generations back.
intro: Our own family sold minerals once, so we know what it feels like to get a letter offering to buy something you'd honestly forgotten you owned. In North Irwin, that's a common story — a small fractional interest tied to a farm that hasn't existed as a working farm since before the interstate went in, still sitting on a deed nobody's looked at closely.

sections.heading: How Small Borough Tracts Get Valued
paragraphs: Westmoreland County is wet-gas Marcellus territory, and a lot of the acreage around North Irwin was leased in blocks that pulled in dozens of small residential and legacy farm parcels together. Because of that, your fractional interest may already sit inside a producing unit even if you've never received a check, which happens when a prior owner leased the interest but it was never properly tracked through an estate transfer.

We check the recorder of deeds records in Greensburg to trace exactly what you own and whether it's currently held by production, then price the interest against recent activity in that unit rather than guessing.

sections.heading: Dealing With Deduction Anger
paragraphs: If you've gotten royalty statements that show a healthy gross number but a net payment that's a fraction of it, you're seeing post-production deductions at work — gathering, compression, dehydration, and marketing costs the operator nets out before paying you. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act sets a 1/8 floor, but it doesn't stop deductions from eating into everything above that floor, and a lot of North Irwin owners tell us they'd rather cash out than keep watching those line items grow.

faqs.question: My deed doesn't clearly separate mineral rights from surface. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, we review the full chain of title to determine whether minerals were severed and who holds them today, which is common with these older Westmoreland County parcels.

faqs.question: Do you charge anything to review my interest?
faqs.answer: No. We review your deed and any lease or royalty history at no cost before making an offer.

faqs.question: What if there's an old lease from the early 2010s still on file?
faqs.answer: That's typical here. We'll factor the existing lease terms into our offer and handle the transfer paperwork with the operator.
